title: Yuvomi
description: Self-hosted family planner: tasks, shared calendar with CalDAV/CardDAV, shopping, meals, budget, notes, contacts and health in one installable PWA on a single SQLite database. Source: https://github.com/ulsklyc/yuvomi

env.name: SESSION_SECRET
env.label: Session secret (optional)
env.description: On a new installation, leave this empty and Yuvomi generates one on its first start, kept in .secrets/ next to the database. To set your own: at least 32 random characters, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32. Changing it later signs everyone out once.

env.name: DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY
env.label: Database encryption key (optional)
env.description: On a new installation, leave this empty and Yuvomi generates one on its first start, kept in .secrets/ next to the database; Settings > Household > Backup and restore shows it, and a backup only opens with it. An installation whose database is already encrypted keeps needing the key it was encrypted with: emptying this field there does not generate a new one, the start is refused. To set your own: at least 32 random characters, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32. Keep a copy either way.

env.name: OIKOS_HTTP_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

env.name: BASE_URL
env.label: Base URL (recommended)
env.description: The address your household uses, e.g. https://yuvomi.example.com. Without it, password reset mails are never sent.

note: On a new installation you can deploy this as it is: Yuvomi generates the session secret and the database encryption key on its first start. Keep a copy of the key - Settings > Household > Backup and restore shows it, and a backup only opens with it. Then open port 3000 (or the one you chose) and create your admin account. Behind an HTTPS reverse proxy, also set SESSION_SECURE=true. All other settings are listed in .env.example.
